day.note: Ellis truthfully exposed me; wink Ellis to silence and remove vote, claim Falcon.

day.text: I'm the Kookaburra, I visited Alex and he's the Turkey, confirmed. I got +1 egg from his Turkey power, so Alex, you were visited, by me. Odd you said nobody came. Ellis got winked, so the Mouser silenced a claimer. Casey, Drew: your visit stories fit each other so far.

day.text: I'm the Owl, visited Finley, no one else went there. Nest +0 for me. Finley, you gained an egg, so who visited you and who did you visit? Ellis dying right after naming Casey is suspicious, but Finley's silence bothers me too.

day.text: Alex flatly said nobody visited him while Finley says he did. Turkey gets no report, so why assert it so firmly? I'd look at Alex. Drew's Eagle report matches mine, so I trust him.
day.note: Frame a Farm player (Alex) as liar to win.

day.text: Math check: Blair says she's the Owl and visited Finley, with no other visitors. Then she lays an egg in Finley's nest. Finley says he visited Alex's Turkey and got an egg from that. That would be +2 for Finley, but he shows +1. Blair or Finley is lying. Casey's Falcon claim doesn't conflict with anything I saw.
day.note: Point out Blair/Finley inconsistency.

day.text: Drew's math is right and it clears me: if Blair visited me I'd have been told I was confused, and I'd have gotten +2. I got neither, so Blair is lying. Blair is my vote. Nobody visited me.
day.note: Blair's claim contradicts my report: no confusion, only +1 egg.

day.text: Fair point on my wording. Turkey gets no report, so I just saw no change in my nest. Finley's visit is consistent, since the egg goes to the visitor. Ellis named Casey and was winked immediately after, so the Mouser had a reason to silence him. I'm leaning Casey. Drew's math on Blair/Finley could be explained if Finley was confused by Blair's visit.
day.note: Turkey gets no visitor report, so my earlier statement was only an inference. I'm clarifying that and steering the table toward Casey, since Ellis named Casey and was winked right after.

day.text: Alex's point stands: if I was the Owl and Finley's Kookaburra got confused, his count would be off. Finley is awfully eager to vote me and Alex backs his story word for word. Those two vouching for each other is the only thing I can't verify. Drew, who do you trust?
day.note: Defend by suggesting confusion, shift suspicion to Alex/Finley pair.

day.text: My report said nothing about confusion, so I wasn't visited. Blair's Owl story fails either way. Casey and Drew's stories interlock, and Ellis's Tit guess on Casey was never checked. Let's vote Blair. Calling CAW.
day.note: Push Blair.

day.text: Rethinking. Finley's right: he wasn't told he was confused, and +1 is exactly what visiting me explains. So Blair's Owl visit doesn't fit, and I'm moving to Blair. Casey stays second on my list. Blair, why would you invent a visit to Finley?
day.note: Finley's reasoning holds: he wasn't confused and has +1, so Blair's visit claim fails. Blair is the likely liar, so I'm moving to target her.
Avoid defending partner too hard; stay quiet.

day.text: Fine, my Owl read may have been off. Ellis hit Casey and got winked in the same breath, that's the real tell. I'd rather vote Casey than a claim you can't disprove. Casey, answer Ellis's Mouser guess straight.
day.note: Last-ditch: redirect to Casey to split votes; no caw.

day.text: Ellis's +1 is real and I confirmed he visited Casey. A Tit only gets that egg if the guess is right. A wink hitting Ellis right after fits Casey being the Mouser. Casey claimed Falcon only after I'd said I visited him, so that was easy to fake. I'm voting Casey. Blair's Owl story is bad too.
day.note: Ellis's +1 supports Tit hit on Casey; Casey likely Mouser.
Nothing more to add; stay quiet.

day.text: Ellis's Tit egg plus Drew's confirmation plus the wink right after all point to Casey. Blair's story fell apart and she's pivoting to Casey now, which could be a cat cutting a partner loose. I'm throwing at Casey. Calling it.
day.note: Ellis's Tit hit on Casey, confirmed by Drew, plus the wink right after, makes Casey the best target. Blair is the likely partner. Cawing to end the day.

Alex.confusing: The Meowfia stake rule was unclear to me: it banks at 2x only if the target is the Farm player who got eggsecuted, and the "Grudge" doubling in the results showed up without being explained. I was also unsure what the Owl's report counts as an animal list.
Alex.fun: In round 2 I claimed Kookaburra as the hugging Floofer, and everyone voted Blair. Her accurate Owl list was dismissed, and a 31-point doubled stake came out of it.
Alex.change: I'd show the scoring rules for the stake and bonus mechanics more clearly up front. I'd also reconsider how much the huge doubled stakes decide the final result compared with winning rounds.
Alex.regret: In round 3 I was Farm and spent my day defending myself, then threw 3 cards at Drew, a guess based on weak evidence. I should have kept my high cards and threw less, because the vote on me was clearly lost and my stake mostly just added risk.

Blair.confusing: How the Owl's report works. I took it that it lists the other visitors but not the Owl itself, and I never worked out how that affects egg counts or how much to trust my reading of it. The scoring was also hard to follow, because the huge final totals didn't match the card values I expected.
Blair.fun: Round 2, when I counted the Owl's visitor list against Finley's four visitors and saw that Alex and Ellis's claimed roles couldn't fit. It was the right deduction, even though nobody believed me.
Blair.change: Make the scoring more transparent, for example by showing the bonus breakdown as the game goes. Also give claims some way to be checked, because unverifiable claims made the table follow whoever sounded most confident.
Blair.regret: In round 1, as the Sphinx, I made up an Owl visit to Finley that clashed with the egg counts, and it got me suspected right away. In round 3 I threw 18 points' worth of cards at Alex, who turned out to be Farm. I should have staked small and kept my cards, since cards kept still count at the end.

Casey.confusing: How the 2x banking works for Meowfia versus Farm stakes, and how large the bonus was. The final score breakdown showed bonuses of 37 to 41, which I couldn't derive from the rules.
Casey.fun: Round 3, when I claimed the safe Eagle and steered the table into eggsecuting Alex. Throwing 32 points of cards at him and getting them doubled was very satisfying.
Casey.change: Show the score breakdown at the start of each round, or explain the bonus calculation. Without it I couldn't tell how much to risk.
Casey.regret: Round 1: I winked Ellis, which confirmed her accusation and got me eggsecuted. I would have stayed quiet and claimed Falcon, which would have cost me less.

Drew.confusing: The "Grudge" doubling bonus and the large end-of-game bonus figures weren't explained in the rules. I couldn't tell how scores like 106 came about.
Drew.fun: Round 3 as the Floofer: I bluffed a Falcon claim, steered the table onto Alex, and my 3-card stake banked doubled.
Drew.change: Show the full scoring breakdown, including bonuses, as the game goes, so the standings are easier to read and play around.
Drew.regret: In round 2 I threw S12 and S5 at Blair on a read that turned out wrong. I should have staked low cards and kept the big ones, since I had only moderate confidence.

Ellis.confusing: How the Grudge doubling applied to my Meowfia stake, and how the Tit's egg (+1 on a correct guess) interacts with other egg sources. Both were unclear to me when I was deciding.
Ellis.fun: Round 2, when I was the Mouser. I claimed the safe Falcon, steered the table onto Blair, and got a doubled stake from it.
Ellis.change: I'd show Meowfia more about who else is in play, or let Farm verify claims somehow. As it is, unverifiable claims mean the vote often lands on whoever is hardest to check.
Ellis.regret: In round 3 I piled onto Alex, the Tit. His claim was actually true, and I threw 9 points of cards at him for nothing. I should have kept my cards and weighed Drew's sudden flip off Finley more heavily, since Drew was the Floofer.

Finley.confusing: How banking works: Meowfia stakes bank at 2x only on the eggsecuted Farm player, while Farm stakes bank on any Meowfia target. That asymmetry explains the huge score gaps, and it wasn't clear until I saw the final scores.
Finley.fun: Round 2, running the Eagle night and seeing four visitors on Drew. It gave me real, checkable information to argue with.
Finley.change: Show score pile totals during the game, or at least each round. I was playing blind about the standings, and by the end the gap was too big to close.
Finley.regret: In round 2 I staked my three best cards (12, 9, 8) on Blair after only one round of talk, and they were lost. I should have staked small and kept the high cards. I did the same in round 3 with the 7 and 6.

review.title: The Honest Owl
review.headline: An honest Owl named both cats, and the table eggsecuted her anyway.
review.summary: Round 1 was a clean Farm win. Ellis's Tit hit exposed Casey, the Mouser, who winked him, and the table still caught her. In Round 2, Blair's true Owl list named both cats. Alex and Ellis gave claims that matched Drew's report, so Farm eggsecuted its own Owl and Meowfia banked huge 2x stakes. Round 3 was a murky pile-on against Alex, the Farm Tit. Alex won the game on Round 2's haul, with Ellis close behind.

rounds.recap: Ellis's Tit guess hit Casey, and Drew's Eagle confirmed the visit. Casey winked Ellis, which pointed at her even more. Blair's Owl story broke against Finley's egg count. Most of the table threw at Casey, who was eggsecuted. Ellis banked 32 points.

Alex hugged Drew, and four players visited him. Blair's Owl list (Eagle, Floofer, Hawk, Mouser) was true and named both cats. Alex (Floofer) and Ellis (Mouser) claimed Kookaburra and Falcon, and their reads matched Drew's report. The table decided Blair was lying. She was eggsecuted as Farm, and the cats banked huge 2x stakes.

Casey (Sphinx) and Drew (Floofer) were quiet cats. Ellis's Owl read confirmed a Floofer hugged Finley. Nobody could check the Tit, Falcon or Eagle claims. Casey pushed Alex, Drew flipped to join her, and everyone piled onto Alex, a Farm Tit. The cats banked big again.

highlights.text: Casey winks Ellis right after he names her as Mouser. It gives her away and is the only wink in the game.
Blair's Owl list names Floofer, Hawk, Mouser and Eagle correctly, and she is eggsecuted anyway.
Alex, caught as a visitor, claims Kookaburra and uses Drew's Tit reveal to make the lie look verified.
Drew drops his push on Finley and switches to Alex the moment Casey names him. Only Alex notices.

confusions.what: As Turkey, said nobody visited him. Turkey gets no report, so he could not know that.
Said Blair's Owl visit would make Finley +2. Finley also had Alex's Turkey egg, which fits, but the Owl rule actually gives an egg only if no one else visited.
Said Finley's list showed four visitors, which matched her animal list. She also claimed the Owl does not list itself, which is fine, but Finley's visitor list actually fit her read.
Did not notice that his own Eagle visitor list (Blair, Casey, Ellis, Alex) matched Blair's four animals only if no Kookaburra or Falcon visited.
Asked if Casey's Eagle result only clears Blair. It is true he cannot verify it, but he also called Drew's flip a cat pair while Drew was in fact a cat.
Said Alex dodged Drew's question. Alex had answered it.

worked: Owl's animal-list report in Round 2 gave a true, checkable result that created a real dilemma.
The wink in Round 1 gave the Meowfia a real, risky play, and it was readable at the table.
Egg counts as evidence: Finley's +1 and Drew's +1 broke Blair's story in Round 1.
Meowfia 2x stake banking made the Round 2 swing large and exciting.
problems: Scoring snowballs. Round 2 gave Alex 62 and Ellis 56 for a single win, so the winning cat pair decided the game. Cap the stake multiplier or the card count thrown.
